tables.name: airports
tables.description: One row per airport on the airline's network.

columns.name: airport_id
columns.doc: Internal number identifying the airport.

columns.name: code
columns.doc: Three-letter code printed on tickets and boarding passes.

columns.name: city
columns.doc: City the airport serves.

columns.name: country
columns.doc: Country where the airport is located.

tables.name: aircraft
tables.description: One row per aircraft in the fleet.

columns.name: aircraft_id
columns.doc: Fleet number identifying the aircraft.

columns.name: tail
columns.doc: Registration mark painted on the aircraft.

columns.name: model
columns.doc: Manufacturer and model name.

columns.name: seats
columns.doc: Number of passenger seats in the cabin layout.

columns.name: max_range
columns.doc: Longest distance the aircraft can fly with a full passenger load, in nautical miles.

columns.name: flight_hours
columns.doc: Flight hours logged since the aircraft's last major overhaul.

tables.name: flights
tables.description: One row per scheduled flight departure.

columns.name: flight_id
columns.doc: Internal number identifying this scheduled departure.

columns.name: flight_no
columns.doc: Public flight number shown on tickets, reused on later dates.

columns.name: origin_id
columns.doc: Airport the flight departs from.

columns.name: dest_id
columns.doc: Airport the flight is scheduled to land at.

columns.name: aircraft_id
columns.doc: Aircraft assigned to the flight.

columns.name: departs_at
columns.doc: Scheduled departure date and time in UTC, written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.

columns.name: status
columns.doc: Outcome code: 1 = landed at the planned airport, 2 = cancelled, 3 = diverted to another airport.

columns.name: arr_delta
columns.doc: Scheduled arrival time minus actual arrival time in minutes, so positive means early and negative means late.

columns.name: passenger_id
columns.doc: Customer number of the passenger.

columns.name: name
columns.doc: Passenger full name.

columns.name: nationality
columns.doc: Nationality shown on the passport.

columns.name: birth_year
columns.doc: Year of birth.

columns.name: tier
columns.doc: Loyalty programme level: 0 = not a member, 1 = silver, 2 = platinum, 3 = gold.

columns.name: points
columns.doc: Current loyalty points balance.

tables.name: bookings
tables.description: One row per ticket sold to a passenger for a flight.

columns.name: booking_id
columns.doc: Ticket reference number.

columns.name: passenger_id
columns.doc: Passenger the ticket was issued to.

columns.name: flight_id
columns.doc: Flight the ticket is for.

columns.name: cabin
columns.doc: Cabin booked: 1 = economy, 2 = business, 3 = premium economy.

columns.name: fare
columns.doc: Price paid for the ticket in euro cents, taxes included.

columns.name: channel
columns.doc: Sales channel code: 1 = airline website, 2 = mobile app, 3 = travel agency, 4 = call centre.

columns.name: booked_on
columns.doc: Date the ticket was bought, written as YYYY-MM-DD.

questions.text: Which cities in Spain are on our network?
questions.sql: SELECT city FROM airports WHERE country = 'Spain'

questions.text: How many flights did we have to cancel in January?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM flights WHERE status = 2 AND departs_at LIKE '2027-01%'

needs_docs.fact: code 2 means the flight was cancelled

questions.text: What was our ticket revenue on flights to New York, in euros?
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(b.fare) / 100.0 FROM bookings b JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = b.flight_id JOIN airports a ON a.airport_id = f.dest_id WHERE a.city = 'New York'

needs_docs.fact: fares are in euro cents, so divide by 100 to get euros

questions.text: Which of our aircraft can fly more than 12,000 kilometres non-stop?
questions.sql: SELECT tail FROM aircraft WHERE max_range * 1.852 > 12000

needs_docs.fact: range is in nautical miles, so multiply by 1.852 to get kilometres

questions.text: Give me the names of passengers who have travelled in business class.
questions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.name FROM passengers p JOIN bookings b ON b.passenger_id = p.passenger_id WHERE b.cabin = 2

needs_docs.fact: code 2 means business class (1 is economy, 3 is premium economy)

questions.sql: SELECT name FROM passengers WHERE tier = 2

needs_docs.fact: level 2 is platinum (1 is silver, 3 is gold)

questions.text: Which planes have flown more than 4,000 hours since their last overhaul?
questions.sql: SELECT tail FROM aircraft WHERE flight_hours > 4000

needs_docs.fact: the hours count only the time since the last major overhaul, not the aircraft's whole life

questions.text: On how many flights did we land later than scheduled?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM flights WHERE arr_delta < 0

needs_docs.fact: the value is scheduled minus actual arrival in minutes, so a negative value means the flight arrived late

questions.text: Tell me how many tickets were sold through travel agencies.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bookings WHERE channel = 3

needs_docs.fact: code 3 means the ticket was sold by a travel agency

questions.text: Which passengers hold a ticket from Lisbon to New York?
questions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.name FROM passengers p JOIN bookings b ON b.passenger_id = p.passenger_id JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = b.flight_id JOIN airports o ON o.airport_id = f.origin_id JOIN airports d ON d.airport_id = f.dest_id WHERE o.city = 'Lisbon' AND d.city = 'New York'

readings.sql: SELECT o.code || '-' || d.code FROM flights f JOIN airports o ON o.airport_id = f.origin_id JOIN airports d ON d.airport_id = f.dest_id GROUP BY f.origin_id, f.dest_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

SELECT o.code || '-' || d.code FROM bookings b JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = b.flight_id JOIN airports o ON o.airport_id = f.origin_id JOIN airports d ON d.airport_id = f.dest_id GROUP BY f.origin_id, f.dest_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Route traffic is measured by the number of scheduled flights on the route.

ambiguous.text: How many passengers are booked on our January flights?

readings.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT b.passenger_id) FROM bookings b JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = b.flight_id WHERE f.departs_at LIKE '2027-01%'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bookings b JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = b.flight_id WHERE f.departs_at LIKE '2027-01%'

resolving_note.text: Passenger counts treat each person once, even when they hold several tickets.

ambiguous.text: What does a ticket to Madrid cost?

readings.sql: SELECT AVG(b.fare) / 100.0 FROM bookings b JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = b.flight_id JOIN airports a ON a.airport_id = f.dest_id WHERE a.city = 'Madrid'
SELECT MIN(b.fare) / 100.0 FROM bookings b JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = b.flight_id JOIN airports a ON a.airport_id = f.dest_id WHERE a.city = 'Madrid'

resolving_note.text: The cost of a ticket to a city is quoted as the average fare actually paid.

ambiguous.text: When was our most recent flight to Athens?

readings.gloss: latest flight that was not cancelled
readings.sql: SELECT MAX(f.departs_at) FROM flights f JOIN airports a ON a.airport_id = f.dest_id WHERE a.city = 'Athens' AND f.status <> 2

readings.gloss: latest scheduled flight, cancelled or not
readings.sql: SELECT MAX(f.departs_at) FROM flights f JOIN airports a ON a.airport_id = f.dest_id WHERE a.city = 'Athens'

resolving_note.text: Cancelled flights are not counted as flights that took place.

ambiguous.text: Who is our most loyal passenger?

readings.sql: SELECT name FROM passengers ORDER BY points DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT p.name FROM passengers p JOIN bookings b ON b.passenger_id = p.passenger_id GROUP BY p.passenger_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Loyalty is judged by the size of the loyalty points balance.
